conflicts.fact: Reflection rule for y = −x, and number of coordinate rules studied
conflicts.versions: Lesson 3 gives reflection in y = −x as (a, b) → (−b, −a) across four mirror lines (y-axis, x-axis, y = x, y = −x). Lesson 8 says its evidence pack contains a table of 'all six coordinate reflection rules studied across Lessons 3–6', but Lesson 3 only has four rules and Lessons 4–6 introduce no new coordinate rules.

conflicts.fact: Which lesson develops the 'cumulative model' and what it contains at each stage
conflicts.versions: Lesson 4's teacher script says Lesson 1 added lines of symmetry, Lesson 2 the concept of reflection, and Lesson 3 coordinate rules, while Lesson 2's model was the matatu diagram with the mirror line, and Lesson 3 says the model came from Lesson 2 with arrows. Lesson 7 says the cumulative model has been 'the annotated Cartesian plane diagram they have been building since Lesson 3', while Lessons 4–6 and 8 say it has been built since Lesson 1.

conflicts.fact: When the four properties of reflection (equidistance, perpendicular connector) were first discovered
conflicts.versions: Lesson 3's overview says learners in Lessons 1 and 2 had already discovered that the image is equidistant and the connector is perpendicular. Lesson 4 presents these as properties discovered for the first time ('shift from rule-following to rule-discovery'), and Lesson 1 and Lesson 2 do not cover them.

conflicts.fact: Which lesson the mirror-line equation work belongs to
conflicts.versions: Lesson 4's overview says the perpendicular-bisector fact will anchor work on mirror-line equations in Lesson 5. Lesson 3 says the equation of an unknown mirror line is set up for Lesson 4, whereas Lesson 5 actually covers it. This is a one-lesson mismatch in the sequence.

conflicts.fact: Number of congruence tests / role of the lessons
conflicts.versions: Lesson 7 describes itself as 'penultimate' and states the four tests, whereas Lesson 6's overview says congruence conditions come in 'the next two lessons' (7 and 8), but Lesson 8 introduces no new tests. Lesson 7's Observe also says each test yields a unique triangle 'sometimes a direct copy, sometimes a mirror-flipped copy', while its Learned says reflection is always opposite congruence.
